question: Can Fix3 (_is_protocol_only_prefix) be redesigned to reject only truly protocol-only prefixes (bare scheme+authority with no path, query, or fragment) without blocking valid host?query parameterization, and does a discriminating test corpus demonstrate its independent necessity over Fix2?
hypothesis: A redesigned Fix3 that checks for '?' or '/' or '#' in the rest after '://' will: (1) correctly reject bare authority prefixes like 'https://api.example.com' (protocol-only), (2) correctly accept query-parameterized prefixes like 'https://api.example.com?key=' (valid parameterization), (3) not break existing kernel tests or HTTP binding, and (4) be independently necessary for patterns where Fix2 passes but Fix3 should reject (bare authority without trailing delimiter).
falsifier: Redesigned Fix3 rejects any valid query-parameterized URL (host?query pattern), OR fails to reject protocol-only bare authority prefix, OR breaks existing kernel regression tests, OR HTTP binding accuracy drops below 1.0 on previously passing endpoints.

baselines.description: Current Fix3 (if '/' not in rest: return True) applied to query-parameterized prefix 'https://api.example.com?key='. Expected: old Fix3 incorrectly returns True (blocks valid parameterization). Demonstrates the bug being fixed.

Literal mechanisms (zero-parameter) with same training data and valid IDs from parent. Expected: 9/9 HTTP execution success. Regression baseline to confirm Fix3 redesign does not break existing capability.

positive_control.description: Redesigned Fix3 applied to query-parameterized prefix 'https://api.example.com?key='. Expected: returns False (does NOT reject), allowing distill_parameterized to proceed. This is the primary fix validation.

null_control.description: Redesigned Fix3 applied to bare authority prefix 'https://api.example.com'. Expected: returns True (rejects), confirming Fix3 still catches truly protocol-only patterns.

measurement_validity: Fix3 redesign implemented in src/spider/kernel.py as a single function body change to _is_protocol_only_prefix; no other function signatures changed
URL test corpus covers 10+ patterns across 4 categories: protocol-only, query-parameterized, path-slash, mixed
Existing kernel regression tests (3/3) run before and after Fix3 change to confirm no regression
HTTP binding test re-run with query-parameterized endpoint (comments?postId=${url}) to verify end-to-end parameterization works for host?query patterns
Discriminating test demonstrates Fix3 independently necessary: protocol-only prefix rejected by Fix3 but not by Fix2 alone (Fix2 passes bare authority in some contexts)
All measurements use committed code (no run_experiment.py harness dependency for Fix3 unit tests)
GET-only endpoints tested (PUT/POST not in scope)
Network access to jsonplaceholder.typicode.com required for HTTP binding test
decision_rule: C1: Fix3 redesigned function rejects bare authority prefix 'https://api.example.com' (returns True)
C2: Fix3 redesigned function accepts query-parameterized prefix 'https://api.example.com?key=' (returns False)
C3: Fix3 redesigned function accepts path-slash prefix 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/' (returns False, same as current)
C4: Old Fix3 (before redesign) incorrectly rejects query-parameterized prefix 'https://api.example.com?key=' (returns True) — demonstrates the bug
C5: Kernel regression tests pass (3/3) after Fix3 redesign
C6: HTTP binding accuracy >= 1.0 on query-parameterized endpoint (comments?postId=${url} with valid unseen IDs postId 5-7)
C7: distill_parameterized with Fix3 redesign produces correct Mechanism for query-parameterized observations (slot ['url'], template 'comments?postId=${url}')
ALL conditions C1-C7 must pass for SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST; any failure triggers FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING
product_consequence_positive: C-PARAM-INHERIT expands coverage to include host?query parameterization patterns (previously blocked by overbroad Fix3). Fix3 is demonstrated as non-redundant defense-in-depth for bare authority patterns. Claim ceiling expands from 'path-slash GET only' to 'path-slash and query-parameterized GET'. Product viability signal strengthened for real-world URL patterns.
product_consequence_negative: C-PARAM-INHERIT remains limited to path-slash URL patterns only. Fix3 either remains overbroad (blocks valid queries) or is redundant (Fix2 already handles all cases). No product promotion. Consider removing Fix3 entirely if redundancy confirmed.
estimated_cost: Low: Fix3 function body change (5 lines), 10+ unit tests for URL corpus, 3 kernel regression tests, 6 HTTP requests to jsonplaceholder (comments endpoint with postId 5-7). No browser automation, no model calls.
expected_information_gain: High: directly resolves the primary blocker from parent experiment (V2_FIX3_OVERBROAD_BLOCKS_VALID_QUERY_PARAM). Either Fix3 can be fixed to handle host?query patterns (positive, expands claim ceiling) or Fix3 is fundamentally redundant with Fix2 (negative, simplifies codebase). Either outcome materially changes the C-PARAM-INHERIT claim and product architecture.
